basis: Inherited platelet aggregation defect; mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish damage to additional organs.
Facial skeletal and oral overgrowth define the condition; dental abnormalities and hemimacroglossia are common. Airway obstruction and hearing loss occur in fewer than 30%.
Lysosomal storage disorder; progressive neurologic dysfunction and visual impairment are common (>30%). Skeletal and visceral disease chiefly characterize type II.
Hyperplastic mucosal lesion arising mainly in the stomach or colon.
Portal venous obstruction with cavernous collateral formation and portal hypertension; the vascular lesion does not establish intrinsic liver damage.
Defined as a chronic neurological pain disorder; pain alone does not establish damage to other organs.
Carcinoma originating in urinary tract urothelium, including bladder, ureter, urethra and renal pelvis.
Site-unspecified smooth-muscle soft-tissue sarcoma; uterine location and Epstein-Barr virus causation cannot be assumed across the concept.
Bone fragility and craniosynostosis define the syndrome; hydrocephalus occurs in 5/6 patients. Proptosis and blue sclerae alone do not establish ocular damage.
Skeletal myopathy with defining ptosis (12/12) and ophthalmoplegia (11/12). Bulbar weakness is muscular and does not establish a separate neural disorder.
Phagocyte immunodeficiency; intrinsic granulomatous colitis affects roughly 30-50%. Pneumonias and abscesses are separately diagnosed infections.
Neoplasm of skull bones and associated structures; neural, orbital and sinus sites are subtype-specific.
Hereditary susceptibility specifically concerns colorectal neoplasia; the label identifies its target organ and does not imply existing cancer or bowel damage.
Benign neoplasm arising in the oral cavity, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Tuberculosis affecting multiple sites; pulmonary infection accompanies multifocal disease in more than 30%. Other organ sites vary.
Skeletal dysplasia; hearing loss 15/16, subglottic stenosis 6/15 and keloids 8/18 support involvement. Cleft palate 5/17 (~29%) falls below threshold.
Neoplasm involving the cauda equina nerve roots.
Direct drug- or chemical-induced liver injury; an immune mechanism is not universal across this spectrum.
Inflammation of the iris and anterior chamber, predominantly immune-mediated; infectious forms also fall within the mechanism axis.
Isolated spermatogenic failure causing azoospermia and infertility; no established endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease.
Neurological movement disorder producing standing-induced tremor; muscle activity and myalgia do not establish structural muscle disease.
Congenital ureteral dilation with common hydronephrosis and reflux; associated urinary infections are separate diseases.
Neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by alternating episodes of hemiplegia.
Nerve agents inhibit acetylcholinesterase, disrupting central, peripheral and neuromuscular function; transient secretions and miosis do not establish other organ damage.
Adipocytic sarcoma typically arising in deep soft tissues; no specific skin or visceral origin is established.
